name: Vietnam (since 1945)
summary: Modern Vietnam: independence declared in 1945, decades of war against France and the United States, reunification in 1976, and rapid growth after the Đổi Mới reforms of 1986.

location.value: The eastern edge of mainland Southeast Asia; capital Hanoi, largest city Ho Chi Minh City.

terrain.value: A long S-shaped country with the Red River and Mekong deltas and central mountains.

climate.value: Tropical monsoon in the south, with cooler winters in the north; typhoons.

resources.value: Rice, coffee (world’s second-largest producer), seafood, rubber and offshore oil.

disasters.value: Typhoons and floods, especially in the centre and the Mekong delta.

urbanisation.value: Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi grew rapidly.

disease.value: Dengue fever; SARS (2003) was contained early; COVID-19.

economicBase.value: Manufacturing for export (electronics, clothes, shoes), farming and tourism.

tradeRoutes.value: A major exporter to the US, China and the EU.

moneyAndTax.value: The đồng; income and value-added taxes.

inequality.value: Poverty fell sharply after 1990, but gaps between rich and poor have grown.

governmentType.value: A one-party socialist republic led by the Communist Party of Vietnam.

succession.value: Leaders are chosen by the Communist Party at its congresses every five years.

institutions.value: The Communist Party and National Assembly.

stability.value: Stable since the end of the border war with China (1979) and the withdrawal from Cambodia (1989).

eliteConflict.value: Competition between party factions, recently through anti-corruption campaigns.

armyAndTech.value: A large army with Soviet and Russian weapons.

majorWars.value: First Indochina War (1946–54), Vietnam War (1955–75), war with China (1979).

territoryChange.value: North and South were reunified in 1976; disputes with China over islands in the South China Sea.

alliancesRivals.value: Historic tensions with China; ties with the US since 1995.

inventions.value: Few internationally known inventions; strong growth in software and electronics.

scienceEducation.value: High literacy and strong school results.

openness.value: The Đổi Mới reforms (1986) opened the economy to markets and foreign investment.

religion.value: Folk religion and Buddhism; many non-religious.

languageWriting.value: Vietnamese in the Latin-based Quốc ngữ script.

artsArchitecture.value: Water puppetry, the áo dài dress, and French colonial and modern architecture.

socialStructure.value: A fast-growing urban middle class; rural poverty in the mountains.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong identity based on resisting foreign rule (China, France, the US).

ideasReligions.value: Communism and Ho Chi Minh Thought; Buddhism and ancestor worship remain widespread.

riseSignals.value: The Đổi Mới reforms (1986) began fast economic growth.

peakPeriod.value: Still exists; fast growth since the 1990s.

declineSignals.value: Not applicable: still exists. Challenges include corruption and environmental stress.

outcome.value: Continues today as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

overallCertainty.value: High for statistics; war tolls are estimates.
